semanticInvariant: The possessor experiences a brief interruption in breathing; no cause, emotion, or intensity is inferred.
testCases: Her breath hitched when the latch clicked.
His breath caught before he answered.
Their breath stuttered at the sudden noise.

semanticInvariant: The possessor's heartbeat is forceful; no speed, emotion, cause, or medical implication is added.
testCases: His heart pounded as the footsteps neared.
Her heart hammered beneath the silence.
My heart thudded once, hard enough to notice.

semanticInvariant: The possessor's eyes become wider; the rule must not infer surprise, fear, recognition, or any other cause.
testCases: Her eyes widened at the figure in the doorway.
His eyes widened, but he said nothing.
Their eyes widened before the screen went dark.

semanticInvariant: The possessor tightens or sets the jaw; no emotion, intention, dialogue, or cause is inferred.
testCases: His jaw clenched at the accusation.
Her jaw tightened, then relaxed.
Their jaw set before they stepped forward.

semanticInvariant: The same fist or fists tighten; no emotion, threat, target, force, or subsequent action is added.
testCases: His fists clenched beneath the table.
Her fists tightened at her sides.
My fists tightened around the folded note.

semanticInvariant: The same subject performs a difficult swallow; no emotion, obstruction, pain, or motive is inferred.
testCases: He swallowed hard before speaking.
She swallowed hard, watching the door.
I swallowed hard and looked away.

semanticInvariant: The possessor's shoulders move or rest lower; no emotion, fatigue, defeat, cause, or intention is inferred.
testCases: Her shoulders sagged when the door closed.
His shoulders sagged, though he remained standing.
Their shoulders sagged beneath the coat.

semanticInvariant: The same subject changes the angle of the same head; no direction, curiosity, confusion, or intention is added.
testCases: She tilted her head toward the sound.
He tilted his head, considering the diagram.
They tilted their head before answering.

alternatives: $1 pressed at the bridge of $2 nose
$1 applied pressure to the bridge of $2 nose
semanticInvariant: The same subject presses the bridge of the same nose; no frustration, fatigue, pain, motive, or ownership of the hand is inferred.
testCases: He pinched the bridge of his nose.
She pinched at the bridge of her nose before replying.
I pinched the bridge of my nose and reread the number.

semanticInvariant: The possessor's voice becomes lower without deciding whether pitch or volume changed; no secrecy, intimacy, emotion, or audience is inferred.
testCases: His voice dropped when the others entered.
Her voice lowered, though the words stayed clear.
Your voice dropped at the end of the sentence.

semanticInvariant: The same silence continues for a noticeable duration; no mood, cause, participants, or consequence is inferred.
testCases: The silence stretched between them.
The silence lengthened, unbroken by the rain.
Silence dragged until the clock chimed.

semanticInvariant: The same scene contains plainly perceptible tension; no source, emotion, conflict, or outcome is inferred.
testCases: The tension was palpable before the vote.
The tension felt heavy, even from the hallway.
Tension was thick around the table.
